gap: Two defects, both found by replaying a session rather than a stage, and one thing this lane could not do. (1) The integrity flag depends on how many packets were lost together. The sequencer stamps the reset for an abandoned gap with the first missing sequence, and qip_orderbook::replay reads every Reset as a venue's completed rebuild: it closes the period and resynchronises on the spot. After a two-packet hole the next packet is not contiguous with the reset, a period opens and never closes, and every later book edit is withheld. After a one-packet hole the next packet is contiguous, no period opens, every step is flagged reliable, and a simulated buy of 450 is filled 111 against a book rebuilt from nothing. Telling a venue's snapshot reset from the cell's own declaration of loss needs the canonical schema (MessageBody::Reset) to say who declared it, or replay to stop treating a reset with no snapshot behind it as a rebuild; the second contradicts qip-orderbook's a_reset_closes_the_period_and_the_messages_after_it_are_reliable_again, so it is a decision and not a patch. (2) A checkpoint that has been stored does not resume to the same state. qip_core::Timestamp serialises to the millisecond (1704153600000005000 ns round-trips through serde_json as 1704153600000000000), VenueCheckpoint carries the last print's venue time and the last update time, and a venue-native session is stamped in nanoseconds. The test's checkpoint arm is therefore held in memory; through serde_json it fails on unmodified code. Making the serialised form lossless changes what every hash over a sub-millisecond timestamp is computed from across the workspace. (3) 'Once more on a different host' is a pinned digest every host recomputes, not a second host in one run. Nothing in a composition root replays venue-native bytes: qip_orderbook::replay has no non-test caller, and the production replay (ReplayAdapter in qip-deepbrain) replays SensedRecords.
verification: cargo test -p qip-acceptance --test tick_replay: 'test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed'. Mutations against the determinism test, each restored byte-for-byte by sha256 and re-run green: a snapshot digest that differs from call to call ('book states differ'); a checkpoint restore that forgets the trade count ('a replay resumed from a checkpoint reached different books'; this one SURVIVED the first version of the test, whose checkpoint was taken before anything had traded, and the checkpoint was moved past the first print with a premise asserting it holds a trade); a deterministic change to the sequencer's gap label and a decoder stamping every event one microsecond late (both 'the replay digest moved'; the second needed the per-event nanosecond stamps added to the digest, because the events alone serialise to the millisecond); a replay that flags nothing ('a book edit after the unrecovered hole was replayed as reliable'). The known-gap test was verified the other way: a mutation that stops a reset making the next packet contiguous failed it with 'a one-packet hole is now flagged'.
notes: Advanced 2026-10-05, not closed. The requirement's check is replay digests and identical integrity flags; the digests hold and the flags are wrong for a one-packet hole, so COMPLETE would be false. Both defects also qualify earlier closures: TICK-040 (downgraded, see its row) and TICK-041 (note added). The Timestamp precision is a qip-core fact with consequences outside this domain (any persisted edge record stamped below a millisecond) and wants its own lane.
